'''Hafiz Rashid Khan''' ({{langx|bn|হাফিজ রশিদ খান}}, born June 23, 1961) is a [[Bangladeshi]] [[Postcolonialism|postcolonialist]] poet, author,<ref name="worldcat">{{cite web |url=https://www.worldcat.org/identities/lccn-n89-249202/ |title=Khāna, Hāphija Raśida |website=[[WorldCat]] |access-date=January 8, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181108224742/https://www.worldcat.org/identities/lccn-n89-249202/ |archive-date=November 8, 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref> editor, journalist and [[Indigenous peoples in Bangladesh|Adibaasi]] researcher. His literary philosophy mostly comes from the practice of the [[Neocolonialism|Neo-colonialism]] and known as [[postcolonialist]] writer and reputed for working in the [[Ethnic groups in Bangladesh|tribal]] area at the [[Chittagong Hill Tracts]] in Bangladesh.{{sfn|Reeyad|Russell|2013|pp=4}} As of 2019, he has authored twenty-five titles, including fifteen poetry and eight criticism.

In 1982 at his twenty one years age his first poetry was published from Chittagong.<ref name="dhakareview">{{cite web |url=http://dhakareview.org/hafiz-rashid-khan-kobita/ |script-title=bn:হাফিজ রশিদ খানের কবিতা |trans-title=Poetry of Hafiz Rashid Khan |website=Dhaka Review |language=bn |access-date=January 8, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170110024837/http://dhakareview.org/hafiz-rashid-khan-kobita/ |archive-date=January 10, 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2018 he published fifteen and the last poetry book titled ''Dinga Bhase Dakshin Samudrey''.<ref name="Polaris">{{cite news |last1=Bakhtiyar |first1=S.M. |script-title=bn:হাফিজ রশিদ খান কবিতার ধ্রুবতারা |language=bn |url=http://www.newschittagong24.com/%E0%A6%B9%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%AB%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%9C-%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%B6%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%A6-%E0%A6%96%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%A8-%E0%A6%95%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B0-%E0%A6%A7%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B0/ |access-date=8 November 2018 |publisher=Newschittagong24.com |date=23 March 2018 |location=Chittagong |format=web |archive-date=1 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200701024119/http://www.newschittagong24.com/%E0%A6%B9%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%AB%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%9C-%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%B6%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%A6-%E0%A6%96%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%A8-%E0%A6%95%E0%A6%AC%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%A4%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%B0-%E0%A6%A7%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%B0/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He received several awards including, [[Chittagong City Corporation Literary Award]] for contributing in Bengali essay, honoured by [[Chittagong City Corporation]] in 2016.<ref name="Polaris"/><ref name="CCC-16-DS"/> He also awarded [[Kolkata Little Magazine Library Award]] by [[Kolkata Little Magazine Library And Research Center]] for editing his  magazine ''Pushpakroth''.

==Biography==
[[File:Shobuj Taposh, Hafiz Rashid Khan & Muhammad Nurul Islam at BNWIKI12 celebration in Chittagong (04).jpg|thumb|Hafiz (center) with poet and philosopher [[Shobuj Taposh]] and diplomat [[Muhammad Nurul Islam]] at [[Bengali Wikipedia]]'s celebration in 2016.]]

Hafiz Rashid Khan was born on June 23, 1961<ref name="ISNI/">{{cite web |url=http://isni-url.oclc.nl/isni/0000000029964015 |title=Hafiz Rashid Khan |website=[[ISNI]] |access-date=January 8, 2017 |archive-date=December 26, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191226055720/http://isni.oclc.org/xslt/DB=1.2//CMD?ACT=SRCH&IKT=8006&TRM=ISN%3A0000000029964015&TERMS_OF_USE_AGREED=Y&terms_of_use_agree=send&COOKIE=U51,KENDUSER,I28,B0028++++++,SY,NISNI,D1.2,Ec5e84bba-31,A,H1,,3-28,,30-41,,43-59,,65-70,,74-75,R207.241.225.227,FY&COOKIE=U51,KENDUSER,I28,B0028++++++,SY,NISNI,D1.2,Ec5e84bba-31,A,H1,,3-28,,30-41,,43-59,,65-70,,74-75,R207.241.232.121,FY&COOKIE=U51,KENDUSER,I28,B0028++++++,SY,NISNI,D1.2,Ec5e84bba-31,A,H1,,3-28,,30-41,,43-59,,65-70,,74-75,R207.241.225.226,FY&COOKIE=U51,KENDUSER,I28,B0028++++++,SY,NISNI,D1.2,Ec5e84bba-31,A,H1,,3-28,,30-41,,43-59,,65-70,,74-75,R207.241.225.236,FY&COOKIE=U51,KENDUSER,I28,B0028++++++,SY,NISNI,D1.2,Ec5e84bba-31,A,H1,,3-28,,30-41,,43-59,,65-70,,74-75,R207.241.232.121,FY |url-status=dead }}</ref> in [[Banshkhali Upazila|Banshkhali]], [[Chittagong]], [[East Pakistan]] (now [[Bangladesh]]). His father was a government employee.{{sfn|Reeyad|Russell|2013|pp=5}} He grew up at Sulakbahar area. Hafiz earned a [[Bachelor of Arts|bachelor]] degree from the [[University of Chittagong]]. He currently served as a journalist at the daily newspaper ''[[Suprobhat Bangladesh]]'' in Chattogram.

==Literary works==
In 1982, Hafiz was published his first poetry ''Jostna Kemon Phutechhe''.{{r|dhakareview}} He works with several literary magazines during his early writings career. ''Renaissance'', ''Dhaner Sheeshe Gaan'', ''Brishti'', ''[[Samujjal Sabatash]]'' since 1991,{{sfn|Reeyad|Russell|2013|pp=10}} and ''Pushpakroth'' since 1993.<ref name="Pushpakroth">{{cite web |title=Pushpakroth |trans-title=Pushpakroth |language=bn |url=http://www.porua.com.bd/publisher/পুষ্পকরথ |website=Porua |access-date=January 8, 2017 |location=Chittagong |archive-url=https://archive.today/20131229202117/http://www.porua.com.bd/publisher/%E0%A6%AA%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%B7%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AA%E0%A6%95%E0%A6%B0%E0%A6%A5 |archive-date=December 29, 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Hafiz married Milattunnesa Khanom in 1995. They have two daughters Naisa Hafiz Khan Oichchhik and Raisa Hafiz Khan Oihik.{{sfn|Reeyad|Russell|2013|pp=8}}
